subject: Literacy
title: A story to share
subtopics: Joining in with a repeated line
objectives: Children will listen to a story with pictures and objects.
Children will join in with a repeated line and actions.
content: Listening to a short story with pictures and objects, joining in with a repeated line, and acting the story.
teachingActivities: Tell the same story all week using objects and a simple repeated line; use a different voice for each character; pause before the repeated line; let children act each part.
learnerActivities: Listen to a short story, join in the repeated line and act the story with actions.
resources: A story with a repeated line: "The Hungry Goat" written by the teacher
A toy goat, a basket, a leaf
assessment: Observe whether each child listens to the story and joins in the repeated line.
expectedOutcomes: Joins in with a repeated line.

lessons.title: The hungry goat
lessons.subject: Literacy
objectives: Children will listen to a short story with pictures and objects.
successCriteria: Listens to the story for a short time
Points to a picture in the story
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can name pictures and objects, join in rhymes and handle a book.
lessons.starter: Hold up the toy goat and say "This is Goat. Goat is hungry. Meh, meh, meh." Ask "What does Goat want?"
teacherActivities: Tell the story: "Goat was hungry. He looked for food. He found a leaf. Munch, munch. Goat was happy." Show a picture for each part.
Tell the story again with the toy goat and let a child feed the goat a leaf.
learnerActivities: Children listen and look at the pictures.
Child points to Goat or says goat.
Child points to the leaf.
Child feeds the goat and says "munch".
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Tell the story: "Goat was hungry. He looked for food. He found a leaf. Munch, munch. Goat was happy." Show a picture for each part. Children: Children listen and look at the pictures.
Step 2. Teacher: Ask "Who is hungry?" and wait. Children: Child points to Goat or says goat.
Step 3. Teacher: Ask "What did Goat find?" Children: Child points to the leaf.
Step 4. Teacher: Tell the story again with the toy goat and let a child feed the goat a leaf. Children: Child feeds the goat and says "munch".

practical.title: Feed the goat
steps: Place the basket of leaves on the mat.
Each child feeds the toy goat a leaf.
practical.safety: Use clean paper or washed leaves and make sure no child puts leaves in their mouth. Wash hands after.

differentiation.support: Hold the goat together and point to each picture.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to tell a friend what Goat found.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

lessons.conclusion: Put Goat to sleep and whisper "Goodnight, Goat."
lessons.homeConnection: Tell your child a short story at bedtime with a toy and point to the pictures.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "listen to a short story with pictures and objects" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

learnerFacing.story: Goat was hungry. He looked for food. He found a leaf. Munch, munch. Goat was happy.

lessons.title: Munch, munch
lessons.subject: Literacy
lessons.subtopic: Joining in with a repeated line
objectives: Children will join in the repeated line "Munch, munch, munch".
successCriteria: Joins in at the right time
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can name pictures and objects, join in rhymes and handle a book.
lessons.starter: Hold up the goat and say "Munch, munch, munch." Ask "Can you munch like Goat?"
teacherActivities: Tell the story again and say the repeated line "Munch, munch, munch" at every page.
Tell the story and pause before the line.
Show each picture and wait for the line.
Let a child be Goat and say the line while the others join in.
learnerActivities: Children listen for the line.
Children say "munch, munch" or mime chewing.
Children say the line at the right time.
Child leads and friends join in.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Tell the story again and say the repeated line "Munch, munch, munch" at every page. Children: Children listen for the line.
Step 2. Teacher: Tell the story and pause before the line. Children: Children say "munch, munch" or mime chewing.
Step 3. Teacher: Show each picture and wait for the line. Children: Children say the line at the right time.
Step 4. Teacher: Let a child be Goat and say the line while the others join in. Children: Child leads and friends join in.

practical.title: Munch with Goat
steps: Sit in a circle with a toy goat.
Say the story and wait for the repeated line.
Pass Goat round and everyone says "munch".
practical.safety: Keep toys clean and large. Supervise turn-taking and do not allow children to put toys in their mouths.

differentiation.support: Say the line together and mime chewing.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to say the line in a quiet voice and a loud voice.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

lessons.conclusion: Say the repeated line one last time and wave.
lessons.homeConnection: Tell the story at home and ask your child to say "munch, munch".
teacherReflection: Which children could show "join in the repeated line "Munch, munch, munch"" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

learnerFacing.story: Goat was hungry. Munch, munch, munch. He found a leaf. Munch, munch, munch.

lessons.title: Acting the story
lessons.subject: Literacy
objectives: Children will act out parts of the story.
successCriteria: Does an action for part of the story
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can name pictures and objects, join in rhymes and handle a book.
lessons.starter: Say "Let us be Goat. Walk like Goat. Meh, meh." Walk on all fours or use a gentle walk.
teacherActivities: Tell the story and show actions for each part: look, find, munch, happy.
Tell the story again and let the children act at each part.
Ask one child to find the scarf leaf.
Let each child take a turn as Goat.
learnerActivities: Children watch and copy the actions.
Children act as Goat.
Child finds the scarf and munches.
Child acts as Goat and friends say "munch".
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Tell the story and show actions for each part: look, find, munch, happy. Children: Children watch and copy the actions.
Step 2. Teacher: Tell the story again and let the children act at each part. Children: Children act as Goat.
Step 3. Teacher: Ask one child to find the scarf leaf. Children: Child finds the scarf and munches.
Step 4. Teacher: Let each child take a turn as Goat. Children: Child acts as Goat and friends say "munch".

practical.title: Be Goat
steps: Clear a space on the mat.
Children walk like Goat, look for a leaf and munch.
practical.safety: Clear the floor and keep children apart so they do not bump. Use soft scarves only.

differentiation.support: Act beside the child and hold hands if needed.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to be the storyteller and say what Goat does.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

expectedOutcomes: Uses actions with the story words
lessons.conclusion: Settle Goat down and say "The end."
lessons.homeConnection: Act a short story at home with your child and use actions.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "act out parts of the story" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Retell with pictures
lessons.subject: Literacy
lessons.subtopic: Joining in with a repeated line
objectives: Children will look at pictures and say words about the story.
successCriteria: Points to a picture from the story
Says a word for what they see
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can name pictures and objects, join in rhymes and handle a book.
resources: Three picture cards: hungry goat, leaf, happy goat
lessons.starter: Show the three pictures and say "Look at Goat’s story. What is happening?"
teacherActivities: Put the pictures on the floor and point to each.
Say "Where is the hungry goat?" and wait.
Say "What did Goat find?" and point.
Let each child tell a friend about a picture.
learnerActivities: Children look and point.
Child points to the hungry goat.
Child says "leaf" or points.
Child says a word and the friend listens.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Put the pictures on the floor and point to each. Children: Children look and point.
Step 2. Teacher: Say "Where is the hungry goat?" and wait. Children: Child points to the hungry goat.
Step 3. Teacher: Say "What did Goat find?" and point. Children: Child says "leaf" or points.
Step 4. Teacher: Let each child tell a friend about a picture. Children: Child says a word and the friend listens.

practical.title: Picture talk
steps: Lay three pictures on the mat.
Each child points to one and says a word.
The group says the repeated line together.
practical.safety: Use large pictures with no sharp corners. Supervise turn-taking.

differentiation.support: Use two pictures and say the word with the child.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to put the pictures in order and say first, then.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

expectedOutcomes: Names the pictures in the story
Says a word about the story
lessons.conclusion: Put the pictures in the basket and say "The end."
lessons.homeConnection: Ask your child to tell you what happened in the goat story.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "look at pictures and say words about the story" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Week 9 story check
lessons.subject: Literacy
objectives: Teachers will observe how each child listens to a story and joins in.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can name pictures and objects, join in rhymes and handle a book.
lessons.starter: Say "Munch, munch" and show three stations.
teacherActivities: Set up three stations: story listening, acting and picture talk.
Tell a short story at each station and wait for the repeated line.
Record each child’s level and take photographs.
learnerActivities: Children rotate every four minutes.
Child joins in and acts.
Children tidy at the signal.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Set up three stations: story listening, acting and picture talk. Children: Children rotate every four minutes.
Step 2. Teacher: Tell a short story at each station and wait for the repeated line. Children: Child joins in and acts.
Step 3. Teacher: Record each child’s level and take photographs. Children: Children tidy at the signal.

practical.title: Story stations
practical.safety: Use soft toys and large pictures. Supervise each station and keep floors clear.

differentiation.support: Provide an adult partner and use one picture.
differentiation.extension: Ask a confident child to tell the story to a friend.

assessment.method: Observe and record Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding for: listens to a story; joins in the repeated line; acts a part.

expectedOutcomes: Has an observation record for Week 9
lessons.conclusion: Say "The end" and wave goodbye to Goat.
lessons.homeConnection: Tell a short story every night and pause for your child to join in.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "Teachers will observe how each child listens to a story and joins in" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?
